chapter: Orrin Blackstone and the record shop
title: Raymond Burke and Orrin Blackstone's Playback
summary: Allen recalls Blackstone's praise of Raymond Burke; Steinau knew Blackstone only from a 1945 Esquire jazz book article and was too shy to approach him.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: well the reason I think we probably were aware of Raymond at least in my case was that uh Orrin Blackstone had told me about him because Raymond was on the very first issue of playback magazine which Orrin put out now you may never have seen that issue no I didn't see the Raymond Raymond you know he yeah Orrin was very interested in Raymond and uh felt that he was one of the unsung heroes and we had that record of slow blues around that Raymond put out himself

I remember the record vaguely and I remember it being good but yeah I didn't I didn't know Orrin actually until you and I met later on yeah that would have been October I think in fact the only thing I think it would have been the only thing I knew of Orrin at that point was I had read in an article I think in the 1945 Esquire jazz book meant an article on collecting records uh describing Orrin's findings in very rare records in junk shops and I was impressed enough that I would not have begun to approach him because I I didn't think I knew enough to talk to the man at that time particularly I think I was feeling that if I didn't have enough knowledge to approach somebody as an equal that they would not have at all be interested in talking to me and I didn't feel like being being turned down
